newsitem.title: NIGERIA: At least 18 killed in Nigerian ethnic clashes.
newsitem.headline: At least 18 killed in Nigerian ethnic clashes.

text.p: The Nigerian oil town of Warri, scene of tribal clashes in which at least 18 people were killed in two days, was under heavy army guard on Tuesday, witnesses said.
"The place is now quiet with heavily armed soldiers patrolling the streets," said one journalist there.

He said Brigadier-General Ibrahim Karmashi, commander of the military task force in Warri, told reporters there that some arrests had been made and that his force was "re-adjusting strategies" to ensure there was no new outbreak of fighting.
More troops had also been moved into the town but markets and many businesses in the town centre remained shut.
Dozens of houses and cars were destroyed in the clash on Sunday and Monday which ended a fragile truce.
The latest clash was triggered by the arrest of a man alleged to have been harassing people in Warri.

In March, Ijaw and Itsekiri tribesmen fought in Warri, where the Nigerian unit of oil giant Royal Dutch Shell has its western division operational headquarters, over the relocation of a local government headquarters.

The army intervened after weeks of mayhem to restore peace and a judicial commission is investigating the causes of the incidents, which took scores of lives and forced Shell to close several oil wells.
A company spokesman in Lagos said on Tuesday that Shell's operations had not been affected by the clashes. "We are not disrupted. We are watching the situation," he said.
Local newspapers said the Itsekiri tribe had pulled out of the judicial commission in protest at the latest clash.
